description: Given two lists of integers a and b of the same, non-zero length, where every element of b is non-zero, return a new list of the same length whose element at index i is the remainder of a[i] divided by b[i]. The remainder is the Euclidean one, which is never negative: it lies between 0 and |b[i]| - 1 even when a[i] or b[i] is negative (for example -10 mod 3 = 2 and -20 mod -7 = 1).
